gaps.sentence: Factory workers are paid ___ at the end of each week.
gaps.hint: pay for manual work, usually weekly
gaps.explanation: 'Wages' are paid weekly, often in cash, for manual or unskilled work; salaries are monthly.

gaps.sentence: She has had a brilliant ___ in politics.
gaps.hint: the whole course of a person's professional life
gaps.explanation: 'Career' is the progress through a working life, especially in one profession; 'job' is one position.

gaps.sentence: There is little ___ that the plan will be approved.
gaps.hint: pattern: little ___ that something will happen
gaps.explanation: 'Possibility that ...' is the standard pattern; 'opportunity' means a situation that lets you do something.

gaps.sentence: We sat ___ to the sound of the waves.
gaps.explanation: 'Listen to' means to pay attention to sound deliberately; after 'sat' the -ing form is needed.

gaps.sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.

gaps.sentence: ___ at this old photo — isn't it amazing?
gaps.explanation: 'Look at' means to direct your eyes towards something; the other verbs cannot be followed by 'at' here.

gaps.sentence: Be careful not to ___ your keys on the bus.
gaps.hint: a verb is needed; meaning: no longer have
gaps.explanation: 'Lose' is the verb (opposite of find); 'loose' is an adjective meaning not tight.
'Besides' means in addition to; 'beside' means next to; 'except' means not including.
